summary: Follow-up on the 2027-08-29 production incident that caused degraded inference latency for Verdant's realtime summarization pipeline. Reviewed timeline, mitigations applied, proposed reliability improvements (autoscale tuning, KV cache retention changes, fallback model route), and agreed on action items and a bench test schedule.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-01 10:00AM PDT | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Grace (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood SRE), Jenna (Verdant SRE), Ravi (Verdant Head of Platform), Elliot (Verdant CTO), Maria (Verdant Legal)

Auto-summary (from recorder): Quick sync after the RCA draft was shared; focus on what mitigations stayed in prod, what still to do, and who's owning bench/validation.

00:00 Samir Patel: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to — I know you got the draft RCA this morning, um this will be a quick follow up to confirm next steps and make sure the mitigations we put in on tuesday are holding

00:18 Jenna Morris: yeah morning, thanks. quick note, performance looks a little better but we still see a tail of elevated p95 around 800ms for some requests, not the 2.3s we saw on monday but still above our targets

00:35 Grace Liu: right, so to recap, on 2027-08-29 we had a sudden increase in long-running requests that caused KV cache churn plus an autoscaler gap — the pod scale down/up timings misaligned with coldstart for the Dedicated pool, and we saw ephemeral GPU memory thrashing during warmup, so tail latency spiked

01:02 Ravi Desai: can I interrupt — when you say KV cache churn do you mean the prefix cache for chat state or the model KV cache? we use prefix caching heavily for the summarization flow

01:10 Grace Liu: ah yeah sorry i should be specific — the model KV cache, so the kv cache got invalidated because of the way the batcher was reassigning shards after a node restart, it looked like we lost hot prefixes and reloaded which caused token regen

01:30 Jenna Morris: got it, that matches what our logs show, lots of rehydrations and then lots of duplicate prep requests to the model

01:55 Diego Ramos: and combined with the autoscaler policy we had (scale down at 2m idle) we saw a window where requests hit nodes that were still cold, so kernel init + quantization path took an extra ~500-700ms each

02:20 Elliot Chen: is that a Redwood runtime issue or configuration on our side? we have limited ability to change some of these autoscale settings in staging vs prod

02:35 Grace Liu: it's both — the default autoscale setting plus the batching policy contributed. we recommended increasing the min-replicas for your Dedicated pool to avoid full coldstart under the 95th percentile of your traffic, and to change the batcher shard assignment to be sticky for 30m to avoid rehydration storms

03:00 Samir Patel: we also pushed an interim mitigation on tuesday: sticky shard assignment and a temporary higher min-replicas, plus a hotpath fallback route to the smaller but lower-latency base model when latency exceeds 1.2s. that reduced customer errors and kept p95 below 1.1s for most flows

03:30 Maria Alvarez: quick legal question — will the fallback to base model change data residency or logging in a way that affects our compliance?

03:42 Grace Liu: no, the fallback model runs in the same Dedicated pool in your VPC and uses the same audit logging and KMS configuration; nothing moves to third-party endpoints

04:00 Jenna Morris: thanks for clarifying. we did spot one curious thing in the logs — a spike of 502s right before the latency spike, almost like a short-lived overload. could that be a kafka ingress issue instead of model side?

04:16 Diego Ramos: we looked at ingress side and there was a transient backlog on their ingress nodes; however the model side also had the cache rehydrate which amplified the problem — so it's likely a combo (ingress + model coldstart)
transcript_continued:
06:10 Grace Liu: note on root cause: primary vector appears to be combined autoscale policy + batcher shard reassignment; ingress backlog was contributing but would not have caused the same tail without the rehydration. evidence: kernel trace timestamps, mem alloc graphs, and sequence of rehydrate log entries in the RCA doc (see link sent in chat).

07:02 Samir Patel: questions i want to make sure we close today — do we agree on the remediation roadmap? 1) permanent change to min-replicas and sticky shard policy, 2) add a pre-warm path for common prefixes, 3) bench test with 1k concurrent to validate autoscale behaviour and KV cache retention, 4) rollout plan with canary to prod.

07:28 Ravi Desai: that's fine but i want clearer SLO targets for the rollout windows; we need a rollback plan if we see degradations during canary

07:45 Grace Liu: agreed — propose we run the bench in our Dedicated staging with your workload replay, hold for 48h, check p50/p95/p99 and error rate; rollback is automatic to previous routing if errors exceed threshold; we will document thresholds in the rollout page

08:10 Jenna Morris: on the bench, can you also include the KV cache snapshot restore test? we want to ensure warmup behaves as expected and not rehydrate too often

08:22 Diego Ramos: yes we'll include KV restore + prefix warming, and we will also capture GPU kernel init times and quantized path latencies

08:38 Maria Alvarez: legal will review RCA once Samir sends final doc, we have questions about retention of the logs we requested earlier and any PI exposure. we'll flag items in the doc

09:02 Samir Patel: ok noted, action owners: i'll send final RCA and consolidated timeline by friday (2027-09-03), Grace will attach perf traces and batching configs by thursday (2027-09-02), Diego will prep the staging bench config and invite Verdant to the run by monday (2027-09-06), Jenna will provide ingress logs for the window by sunday (2027-09-04). Maria will confirm legal questions after doc review.

09:45 Grace Liu: small callout — we discovered a micro-optimization that could help: reduce batch size ceil for requests with < 128 token windows to lower kernel init overhead during warmup; we can test that in bench too

10:10 Ravi Desai: how invasive is that change? we don't want regressions for bulk jobs

10:20 Grace Liu: it's configurable per route, so we can apply it only to the realtime summarization route; won't affect bulk jobs that use different endpoints

10:40 Elliot Chen: i'm generally ok with the plan, want to see bench results before broad rollout. thanks for quick turnaround.

10:55 Samir Patel: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with invites and the doc. recap in chat after this.

11:05 Meeting end

References shared: RCA draft (link in chat), kernel traces zip (will be shared by Grace), bench config (will be attached to invite).
